title: The adapter satisfies the mail-adapter interface named by the shipped magic-link blueprint's TAC-504
description: The Resend send adapter exposes exactly the `send({ to, subject, textBody, htmlBody })` method the magic-link blueprint's `TAC-504-security-auth-magic-link-email-delivery-adapter` names, and resolves the fixed outcome shape `{ ok, providerStatus, providerMessageId, error }` on every call. No other method is added to the auth-facing surface; provider status codes and provider message ids are normalised into the four declared fields inside the adapter. A project composing this blueprint alongside the magic-link blueprint wires the adapter reference into the auth routes at composition time and calls `adapter.send` directly.
rationale: The mail-adapter contract is the mandate the auth flow gates on; this blueprint's only reason to exist is to fill that mandate with a shipped default a project can apply and rely on. A shape that differs from TAC-504 leaves the auth routes unable to call the adapter without a project-authored shim, which defeats the shipped-default posture. Normalising provider-specific vocabulary inside the adapter keeps the auth code provider-neutral.
